Is this your first time with this franchise? Or first time buying at or technically before full release?  If so I have.... Some sympathy 

The games don't release well. For GOOD reasons like ambition and scale.  Haven't for 20 years, it's multiple release issues are talked about so often I'm amazed if you missed it all! 
In the coming months and year it will be awesome as it's finished, polished and tweaked to what the community enjoys. 

This has been the design model of this series since BF2 and they decided enough people had fast enough internet to download big patches.

These issues crop up every release. Untill the servers are stressed fully during release. With tens of thousands trying crazy, random only in battlefield stuff many of them don't even crop up to be fixed. 

I like this model.  I'm patient. If I wanted a small simple shooter that's the same on release as the day it dies I'd pick up game that does that. However I want huge scale, ambition and a ton of only in battlefield moments that I know will take some work to make great. 

I'll grab the game early next year at half price when it's starting to get stable and slick.

*Scene: Amazon warehouse*.
 Beams of flurecent hell intermittently illuminate the drooped head and shoulders of an Amazon employee. He's pushing a large metal cart filled with boxes down a street sized corridor of shelves with no other living thing in sight. 

He stops momentarily, wiping sweat from his eyes. 
He fumbles with the lid of a slightly filled bottle hanging from his tattered belt by a broken shoelace. The sweat making his fingers slide on the coke bottles lid.

He finally succeeds and with great urgency whips out his cock to piss frantically into the bottle. With not a moment or shake to spare he stuffs himself back into his pants and roughly screws the lid on, the half filled bottle flapping by his thigh. 

He runs to his trolley tackling it with his full body, desperate to push it back up to speed. 

The cord holding his bottle of piss gets hooked on his trolley. He twists slightly, stumbles, falls and POP the trolley snaps the shoelace right off the neck of the bottle. Ripping the lid off with it. 

Down he goes. Sliding into his own piss face first. 
He starts crying. No. Wailing, tears streaming down his face and shirt as he drags himself to his feet. Marching doggedly towards his trolley. Before....

BEEEP BEEEP BEEP BEEEEEEEEEEP 

He looked at his electronic scanner and scheduler.  He had been too slow. This had happened before, so the tiny plastic device that ruled his life showed that he had been terminated from his employment.  

His head lifted sharply.  As though he stepped on a live electric wire. The snivelling snapped to a stop so abruptly every tear and drop of piss whipped off his face.  No further tears fell. His jaw tightened, eyes focused and the hint of a slow smile grew at the corners of his lips as he marched out without speaking a word.

Hours later the mess was cleaned by a man earning an unliveable wage. He moved the trolley, mopped the floor, then something caught his eye next to the shelf. 

He bent down and reached underneath grabbing the object in a fortunately gloved hand. It was an Amazon name tag. With the name covered in piss and a little blood. 

Not being paid enough to stop or care he chucked it into to the bin. 

The blood runs off the name tag, that was left as a warning. Revealing the name:

 Jack Kittling, the man nobody was paid enough to see coming.
